# Simon Depussay (シモン デプセ)

> Franco-Swiss iOS & web developer based in Tokyo, Japan. Builds iPhone apps in Swift and cloud backends on Microsoft Azure. Native French speaker, JLPT N2 (Japanese), TOEIC 925 (English). Currently studying at HAL Tokyo (2026–2028) and open to internships and jobs.

Contact: depussay.simon@icloud.com
GitHub: https://github.com/simondepussay
Website: https://simondepussay.com (Japanese and English)
The website also has an AI assistant that answers questions about Simon.

- 2024: started using AI as an assistant (GPT-4o).
- Now: builds with Claude Code as a coding agent. Simon designs the architecture, makes the decisions, reviews and tests the code, and ships it.

## Projects

- [Kanji Otter — How it's built](https://simondepussay.com/kanji-otter.html): iPhone app to learn JLPT kanji (N5 to N1), developed since 2024 and improved with user feedback, 600+ downloads, 6 languages. Swift app with offline-first progress, accounts with Microsoft Entra External ID, cloud save through an Azure Functions API (Node/TypeScript) and Azure Cosmos DB, StoreKit 2 subscriptions, Google AdMob rewarded ads, Firebase Analytics. The same structure is reused for two more apps in progress (English vocabulary, Japanese grammar).
- [Kanji Otter on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/jlpt-kanji-otter-adventure/id6497395953)
- [JLPT Étude — How it's built and run](https://simondepussay.com/jlpt-etude.html): web app that builds a daily JLPT N1 lesson (3,315 words, 1,232 kanji, 90 grammar points, French and English). Planning from the exam date and study days per week, spaced repetition, real-pace detection. Serverless on Azure (Static Web Apps + Azure Functions + Blob Storage), offline first, Google sign-in without passwords, ETag conflict merge between devices. 62 automated tests run before every deploy, post-deploy verification, PR preview environments, rollback measured at 2 minutes, 30-day versioned backups, health check every 30 minutes, Application Insights. Built with Claude Code as a coding agent.
- [Methodolodys — How it was migrated](https://simondepussay.com/methodolodys.html): migration of methodolodys.ch, a free learning-resources site for children with dyslexia built over 10 years by a special-needs teacher in Switzerland, from WordPress + Divi to a static site. 1,920 resources and 63 pages migrated without loss; 1,909 downloadable files (5.3 GB: PDF, PowerPoint, Word, video) on Azure Blob Storage, pages on Azure Static Web Apps (HTML/CSS/JavaScript, no framework). Python pipeline reading the .wpress backup and MySQL dump, parsing Divi shortcodes, repairing broken links and mojibake file names, generating previews; 71 old URLs 301-redirected; every link and all 1,909 downloads verified by script. Why: technical debt (PHP and MySQL past end of life, 7 plugins), security (no admin login or database to attack), speed (server time per page from 1.1–1.5 s to about 7 ms), and easier navigation (search, one page per topic, reading settings with the OpenDyslexic font). Test version waiting for the owner's review. Code: https://github.com/simondepussay/methodolodys-static-site
- [Kota Illustrator website](https://gray-cliff-055dc5d00.5.azurestaticapps.net/): artist website for the Japanese illustrator こた, responsive (desktop and smartphone), Azure Static Web Apps.
- [Porco Rosso fan website](https://ambitious-rock-08ecb2600.5.azurestaticapps.net/): fan website for the Studio Ghibli film 紅の豚, desktop format, Azure Static Web Apps.
- [This portfolio](https://simondepussay.com): Node.js on Azure App Service, with an AI assistant on Azure OpenAI using a managed identity (no secret keys).
